findings.reason: Confirmed (high). E43, confirmed by the extraction's review, corrects the proof of Lemma 4.3 (p. 1273). In the paper's conventions π has weight λ_{τ,i} = +λ_τ, and the slope identities read val_l(ι⁻¹φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{nλ_τ}), and with jλ_τ for the j-th partial product. The operative items were not updated. Item 087 still says 'the weight of π has λ_{τ,i} = −λ_τ' and requires ∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{−jλ_τ}. Item 088 states that r_{l,ι}(φ_π) has Hodge–Tate weight nλ_τ, then concludes val_l(ι⁻¹φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏ τ(ϖ_v)^{−nλ_τ}), the sign E43 removes. Item 088's note even says it was 'Corrected by the review'. The red team's check is right: a character with Hodge–Tate weights h_τ has local values of valuation +Σ h_τ val_l(τ(ϖ_v)), and the norm character (Galois realisation ε, weight −1, local value q_v⁻¹) fixes the sign. Since 087–088 feed ordinary automorphy on the main path to Theorem 1.1, the stated formulas are false as written. The fix, propagating E43 into both statements, their proof outlines and item 135's parameter, is right.

Confirmed (high). On p. 1268 (§4, choice of N) the paper requires F_{l²}F′ ⊂ F_l(ζ_N), where F′ is 'the finite field generated by all the m-th roots (hence n-th roots) of elements in the field F_{l^s}'; item 073 records this. Items 076 and 078 weaken it to 'an m-th root of every element of F_{l^s}'. Item 076(iv) then concludes that k(λ) contains all n-th roots of unity, which does not follow. I checked the red team's example with exact arithmetic. N = 7381 = 11²·61 is odd, prime to 21 and above 800. 3⁵ ≡ 1 mod 121 and 3⁵ ≡ −1 mod 61, so 3 has order 10 mod N and k(λ) = F_{3^10} ⊃ F_9. Since 3^10 − 1 = 59048 is prime to 7, seventh powering is bijective on k(λ)^×. So every element of F_3 has a seventh root in k(λ), but μ_7 ⊄ k(λ). The extra condition N ∤ 3⁵ + 1 = 244 holds. So 076(iv) is false under its stated hypotheses, and 078's call to item 014 lacks its hypothesis. The fix, requiring all m-th roots (or μ_m ⊂ k(λ)) as on p. 1268 and in route 13, is right. It is separate from E5.

Confirmed (high). The companion arXiv:2103.00106v1, Remark 1.2 (p. 2), says maximal unipotence of ρ_s(γ_∞) 'is satisfied when 0 ∈ {a_1, …, a_N}'. Item 139 adopts this as a sufficient condition, and item 105's note repeats it. The criterion cannot be right, because it is not intrinsic. On H_0 = {∏ξ_i = 1}/μ_N the character ∏ξ_i^{a_i} is unchanged by a_i ↦ a_i + c, so every character has an exponent vector containing 0, and the remark would make every eigenpiece maximally unipotent at ∞. That fails already for N = 4. The Dwork quartic pencil has generic Picard number 19, so its transcendental part is the rank-3 invariant piece. The other 18 dimensions of primitive H² are algebraic, with finite monodromy, and they are spread over at most 15 nontrivial characters, so some non-invariant eigenpiece has rank at least 2 and is not maximally unipotent. I did not re-derive the red team's rank-two N = 5 example from A'Campo's Jordan-block formula, but it is consistent with this. Qian's own family is covered by Corollary 3.5 (item 049), and item 105 is off the path to Theorems 1.1 and 1.4. The fix is right: remove the clause, record a source issue for Remark 1.2, and keep the maximal-monodromy hypothesis.
